episodes.204384: Hot and humid conditions beneath adequate wind shear from a passing weak upper wave combined with lift from a outflow boundary to initiate scattered strong thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 16th, with embedded severe cells impacted Fountain County and Hancock County.  Later in the evening, more organized strong to severe storms produced damage from eastern Madison County into northern portions of the Indianapolis Metro;  and then very early on the 17th, down to south-central Indiana, with one person injured while camping in Monroe County.  A total of 19,927 power outages occurred in central Indiana, including 7,468 in Hamilton County and 6,473 in Marion County.
episodes.204393: A series of weak, mainly convectively induced disturbances, resulted in the development of thunderstorms during the evening hours. Plenty of CAPE existed, but overall shear was weak, limiting organization.
episodes.204408: Typical summertime pulse thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on August 17, 2025. While most storms remained below severe limits, a severe wind gust of 58 mph occurred in Howell County, with reports of multiple trees down in Pulaski County as well.
episodes.204424: Scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of August 17, 2025. These thunderstorms were non-severe, but did produce gusty winds. One thunderstorm near Celina produced minor tree and power pole damage.
episodes.204491: A traditional monsoon flow on the western flank of an upper level high over the central U.S. combined with daytime heating resulted in the development of shower and thunderstorm activity across the higher terrain during the early through late afternoon hours. Some of this shower and thunderstorm activity moved over the South Fork burn scar on both August 17th and August 18th resulting in flash flooding and debris flow across roadways on and downstream of the burn scar. Overall impacts were reported to be more severe and widespread on August 17th compared to August 18th. Finally, a brief landspout was observed in Las Vegas during the mid afternoon on August 18th as well as near the Bernalillo and Sandoval County line during the mid afternoon on August 19th.
episodes.204578: Hot weather resulted in daily episodes of clusters of storms with damaging winds, isolated hail, and some areas of flash flooding from August 12 through August 18th.  The most widespread activity occurred August 15th, and 18th, when several lines of storms moved through the area.  While isolated, the evening of the 16th saw the largest hail in this period, with a supercell producing hail up to 3 inches in diameter in far northeast Stephenson County, Illinois.
episodes.204584: Hot weather resulted in daily episodes of clusters of storms with damaging winds, isolated hail, and some areas of flash flooding from August 12 through August 18th.  The most widespread activity occurred August 15th, and 18th, when several lines of storms moved through the area.
episodes.204612: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of the 17th with convective temperatures breached by mid-afternoon. Although the environment was not favorable for severe storms with warm mid-level temperatures, a relatively dry sub-cloud layer allowed a few of these storms to produce severe wind gusts. The most notable storm occurred over the city of Lubbock where a peak wind gust of 77 mph was recorded. This storm also damaged an apartment complex in the city of Lubbock by ripping off the roof. The high amounts of moisture within the cloud bearing layer also allowed these storms to create heavy rainfall which caused flash flooding in the city of Lubbock.
episodes.204711: A cold front approaching from the Great Lakes during the morning hours of August 17, 2025 continued to advance into central Pennsylvania during the late morning to early afternoon hours. Ample forcing associated with the cold front coupled with sufficient instability, and a pocket of relatively dry air in the lower-levels allowed for isolated instances of damaging winds across the southern tier of Pennsylvania where shear remained marginally sufficient for thunderstorm development.
episodes.204738: A couple clusters of severe thunderstorms impacted western and northeastern Maryland.
episodes.204741: Clusters of thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced widely scattered instances of gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.204986: Numerous pulse thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of August 17th. A high instability and low shear environment made conditions conducive for microbursts. Two of these microbursts became severe and produced localized wind damage in Franklin and St. Louis counties.
episodes.205223: With hot temperatures in place, afternoon pop up thunderstorms lead to isolated microbursts across central and portions of northern Arkansas.
episodes.205397: Scattered showers and storms moved across the region during the afternoon as a front crossed the region. Most convection was sub-severe early on with meager CAPE and effective shear, however, convection intensified east of Pittsburgh as the ongoing convection encountered a more unstable air mass. Damaging winds were the only threat with convection.
episodes.205445: Intense thunderstorms brought heavy rainfall and a debris flow east of Sula.
episodes.205593: A wet August resulted in renewed minor to locally moderate river flooding along portions of the middle Big Sioux River.
episodes.205770: During the afternoon and evening of the 16th, a series of severe thunderstorms produced widespread damaging winds and instances of severe hail around the western and northwestern Chicago metro area.
episodes.205921: The Michigan City C-MAN station recorded a 40 kt gust as thunderstorm outflow moved over during the evening of the 16th.
episodes.206141: Diurnal multi-cell thunderstorms produced observations of severe winds (and wind damage) across western and central Oklahoma on the 17th.
episodes.206260: A series of thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall and widespread flooding to much of the Chicago metro area, namely the south and west suburbs and up into the city of Chicago. Several Oswego District 308 schools received water and storm damage. Flood damages were estimated at around $288 million across the metro area, most of which came from the city of Chicago which alone accounted for roughly $230 million in damages with roughly 40,000 individual structures flooded around the city. The remainder of Cook County accounted for roughly $57 million in flood damages with more than 10,000 additional structures flooded. Several instances of wind damage were also reported, mostly damage to trees.
episodes.206295: Although upper level ridging was in place, weak disturbances moving through the ridge resulted widely scattered showers and thunderstorms August 16 and 17. The stronger storms, which formed in deep inverted-V environments, resulted in a few instances of severe gusts, mainly across the eastern plains.
episodes.206333: Thunderstorms produced strong winds and torrential rainfall over portions of northwest Indiana during the night of the 16th.
episodes.206334: During the evening of the 17th, a strong thunderstorm brought torrential rainfall to parts of LaSalle County.
episodes.206493: Rounds of strong to severe storms throughout the day on August 16th resulted in instances of large hail, damaging winds and flash flooding in western Wisconsin. Hail with these storms reached up to golf ball sized near New Lisbon along with instances of tree damage. Later into the evening, additional storms moved through Grant County and produced heavy rainfall leading to flash flooding in Lancaster along with some quarter sized hail.
episodes.206512: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across Northern Louisiana during the late afternoon and early evening on August 17th. As these thunderstorms and the associated outflow boundaries moved southwest, they encountered increasing instability with temperatures in the upper 90s to near 100 degrees and dewpoints in the lower 70s, yielding 3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Despite the stronger instability, shear was quite weak. This weak shear resulted in very unorganized storms with numerous strong outflows. Strong storm cores supported the threat for microbursts, particularly where outflow boundary collisions occurred. As a result, a few thunderstorms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts across portions of Northeast Louisiana.
episodes.206554: A few thunderstorms developed in northern NJ, producing frequent lightning. Some damage from a lightning strike was reported.
episodes.206582: Heavy rain during the middle of August resulted in minor river flooding along the Cedar River and on both Turtle and Dobbins Creeks.
episodes.206744: Several individual rounds of thunderstorms impacted southern Minnesota from Friday, August 16th through Sunday, August 18th. Heavy rain amounts on the order of 5-10 inches fell over the course of 72 hours, most of which fell from late Saturday into early Sunday, leading to several cases of flooded roadways and damaged buildings. The highest amounts and most widespread impacts were across Waseca County.
episodes.206859: Convection along the retreating Gulf breeze produced waterspout activity on the evening of August 16, 2025.
episodes.206865: An upper level disturbance and nearby stationary front led to multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms across southern WI. Large hail and damaging straight line winds led to trees down and some structural damage.
episodes.206880: Brief but intense heavy rainfall from thunderstorms, on top of weeks of wet weather, resulted in additional flooding across Marshall, Hamlin, Codington, and Deuel counties starting on the 17th and persisting well into the 18th.  An estimated 3 inches of rain fell in Lake Poinsett, while 1.63 inches was recorded by the COOP sensor 20 miles north northeast of Aberdeen, 1.62 inches was submitted by the CoCoRaHS volunteer in Claremont, and 1.5 inches by the CoCoRaHS observer in Hayti. Flooding was most prominent in urban areas such as Aberdeen where multiple roads and intersections flooded. Clear Lake and Lake Poinsett would also see significant water issues.||These storms would also generate sporadic strong winds, with a gust of 63 mph recorded at the Aberdeen Regional Airport.  A 61 mph gust was recorded by the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 4 miles west of Trail City, and a gust to 62 mph at the South Dakota State University mesonet station near La Plant.
episodes.206905: During the overnight, a slow moving convective cluster within an environment with a strong low-level jet and abundant deep-layer moisture slid from western to southern Minnesota. Storms continually regenerated on the southwest flank of the cluster, with a boundary remaining stationary for several hours from south of Marshall to north of Westbrook. Some areas had more spotty heavy rainfall the prior night, and new rainfall amounts were generally from 2 to 4 inches in the band with radar estimates between of 4 to 6 inches. Numerous city and some rural roadways were inundated.
episodes.207019: A nearly stationary thunderstorm on the afternoon of August 16th, 2025 caused flash flooding in the Tucson Metro. Water flooded the streets from curb to curb, roughly 6 inches of moving water, occurred in multiple locations. A nearby rain gauge reported 1.26 inches of rainfall fell in less than 1 hour.
episodes.207052: With the approach of a shortwave aloft and a pre-frontal trough showers and thunderstorms were able to spark in an unstable environment characterized by about 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE. One storm was able to become severe and produce isolated damaging winds.
episodes.207141: A weakening cold front moved through western and north central New York from the early morning through mid afternoon hours, only producing one early-morning severe storm across southwestern New York State.
episodes.207142: A cold front moved across Lake Erie during the early morning hours, resulting in gusty winds up to 48 knots across portions of the lake.
episodes.207160: The combination of strong instability and strong wind shear resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across portions of the Concho Valley and Northern Edwards Plateau on the afternoon of the 19th. A few severe storms also occurred on the 17th. The storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.207184: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi during the afternoon and evening hours of August 13th through 17th. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with the strongest of storms.
episodes.207191: Major Hurricane Erin moved northeast and north of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Erin's Outer Bands and then Feeder Bands still affected the islands, producing strong thunderstorms, gusty winds, and heavy rains across the islands. Several reports of wind gust damage, along with reports of high surf, flooding and debris flow were received between August 16 to 18.
episodes.207214: Thunderstorms produced Flash Flooding across the area. Rainfall rates between 0.75 inches to 1.25 inches in one hour.
episodes.207315: High-based thunderstorms across southern Montana consistently produced gusts up to 66 mph.
episodes.208204: A warm front was draped across northern Iowa the afternoon and evening of August 17th. Convection developed along the boundary late in the afternoon in a deeply unstable environment with over 4000 J/kg of MLCAPE. Shear was lacking an prevented storm organization and more robust development, with around 25 kts of effective shear. Low level CAPE was high at over 200 J/kg in the 0-3 km and allowed for stretching of the updraft, resulting in a brief tornado in northern Iowa. This tornado remained over cropland and did not result in tree or structural damage, hence the EF-unknown rating.

Roughly 40,000 structures sustained flood damage around the city of Chicago. The greatest impacts were felt across the southwest side near and east of Midway Airport, but reports came in from all across the city. Chicago alone accounted for approximately $230 million in flood damages.
Approximately 500 structures were flooded in Chicago's west suburbs, including Northlake and Maywood, totaling about $2 million in damages.

The Big Sioux River near Estelline rose above flood stage on the morning of August 17th, cresting around 2.53 feet above flood stage (1646.53 ft) on August 19th. This crest is in the moderate flood category. The river then fell below flood stage on the morning of August 28th.
Multiple trees and power lines were reported down in Markham.
Multiple reports of flooded basements came out of Chicago's Greater Grand Crossing community area.

Widespread flash flooding impacted the southwest side of Chicago. The city received over 3,000 service requests for water in basements, a large majority of which were from areas near and east of Midway Airport. The highest concentration of reports were out of the West Lawn, Chicago Lawn, Marquette Park, and Gage Park community areas. A photo shared via social media showed at least six inches of standing water on roads and sidewalks in Gage Park. Near W 47th St and Archer Ave, at least four cars were stranded in a flooded viaduct. Another viaduct was flooded at 75th St and S Western Ave in Beverly View. By the morning of the 17th, 24-hour rainfall reports from around the area ranged between two and three inches.
A private weather station recorded 4.94 of 24-hour rainfall, 4.46 of which fell between 2 and 6 AM CST.
A private weather station in southwest Aurora recorded 5.66 of 24-hour rainfall, 4.88 of which fell between 2 and 6 AM CST.
A private weather station in Oswego recorded 6.02 of 24-hour rainfall, 5.42 of which fell between 2 and 6 AM CST.
Flood damages were estimated at $55 million as around 10,000 structures flooded across Chicago's near southwest suburbs, including Riverside, Berwyn, Cicero, and Summit.
An estimated 20 structures were flooded in southern Kane County, specifically in the Aurora and Montgomery areas, amounting to roughly $15,000 in damages.

At least two cars were stuck in floodwaters underneath a viaduct at E 95th St and S Cottage Grove Ave in Cottage Grove Heights. At least one was towed out.

A photo shared via social media showed floodwater up to one foot deep along 131st Pl in Whiting.

Significant flooding was reported around parts of northern Will County, namely in the vicinities of Joliet, Romeoville, and Plainfield. In Joliet, Caton Farm Rd was closed at Joe Adler Dr, and IL Rt. 53 was closed at a viaduct south of Caton Farm Rd due to flooding. A car was reported stranded in floodwater near Center St north of I-80 in Joliet. In Crest Hill, street flooding was reported at IL Rt. 53 and Theodore St. Standing water was reported at IL-126 and County Line Rd in Plainfield. An estimated 250 structures were flooded in this area amounting to around $1 million in flood damages.
Seven to ten large tree limbs were downed at Long Beach Elementary. Time was estimated based on radar.
A lightning strike impacted Oswego East High School knocking out electrical systems including telephones. The time of the strike is unknown and was estimated using radar and lightning data.

Significant basement flooding was reported in Boulder Hill. A car was also reported floating in floodwater. One private weather station in town recorded 5.1 of 24-hour rainfall on the morning of the 17th, and another recorded 4.5.
Three to four feet of standing water were reported in Oswego's Fox Chase subdivision.

At Oswego High School, prolonged intense rainfall overwhelmed the capacity of a storm drainage system. Up to two feet of water flooded a courtyard near the school. Water flowed from the courtyard into the school via a set of double doors and reached depths of 8 to 10 inches near the entrance to the building. Water proceeded to flow into hallways, athletic facilities, and the gymnasium. The damage required the gym floor to be replaced. Damages amounted to over $300,000, with the gym floor alone costing around $250,000.

Torrential rainfall led to the failure of a drain pipe coupling at Oswego East High School. The failure took place on the third floor of the school causing water damage to spread to the lowest three levels. Hard ceilings had to be redone, carpets were extracted and cleaned, drywall was repaired, and lower insulation was replaced. Damages totaled between $200,000 and $250,000.

Long Beach Elementary in Boulder Hill experienced water damage following prolonged heavy rainfall. Water entered the building via an existing leak in an old cast iron drain pipe. Most impacts were to one classroom and a portion of the school was closed while repairs were made. Drywall and insulation had to be replaced and the damaged drain pipes were replaced with new PVC pipes. Repairs totaled about $30,000.
